title: Continuous Manufacturing and Advanced Control
answer: Continuous manufacturing runs material through without stopping between steps, which depends on real time monitoring and control, a natural place for AI models. ICH Q13 sets the international expectations for continuous manufacturing of drug substances and products.

reading.body:
Continuous manufacturing depends on real time monitoring and control, which makes it a natural place for AI models. ICH Q13 sets the international expectations for continuous manufacturing of drug substances and products.

The mechanism is straightforward. Batch manufacturing holds material between steps for testing. Continuous manufacturing feeds raw materials in and product out without stopping, so the process has to be kept in its target state as it runs. That requires measuring quality attributes during manufacturing, which is what process analytical technology does, and estimating quantities that are hard to measure directly from other process measurements, which is what a soft sensor does. AI fits in both roles.

The regulatory consequence is the part that changes engineering decisions. Because control models become part of the control strategy, they must be described in the filing and validated accordingly. A model that estimates a quality attribute is not an internal convenience in this setting. It is part of the argument that the process produces conforming material, and it carries the documentation and validation burden that follows from that.

What the data does not cover is how any of this performs in practice. It names no vendor, no plant, no model architecture, and no measured outcome. The only dated item is ICH's adoption of Q13 in November 2022. The rest is definitional: what continuous manufacturing is, what the two named technologies do, and where the regulatory line falls.

explainer:
Batch manufacturing makes a product in discrete lots, with material held between steps for testing. Continuous manufacturing feeds raw materials in and product out without stopping, which can shrink equipment, cut cycle times and improve consistency. It depends on real time monitoring, often through process analytical technology, and on control systems that keep the process in its target state.

AI fits here as soft sensors that estimate quality attributes from process data, as models that detect disturbances and divert nonconforming material, and as advanced controllers. ICH Q13 sets international expectations for continuous manufacturing, including how to define batches, control strategy and material traceability. Because control models become part of the control strategy, they must be described in the regulatory filing and validated accordingly.

What continuous manufacturing is

Most medicines are still made in batches: a quantity of material moves through each step, stops, is tested, and moves on. Continuous manufacturing runs material through the steps without stopping, with sensors measuring quality as it flows and controls adjusting the process in real time. Regulators have encouraged it because it can be more consistent, more flexible and faster to scale, and several approved medicines are now made this way.

Where AI fits

Continuous lines depend on advanced process control: models that read sensor data, predict product attributes and adjust settings to keep quality within limits. Classical control uses fixed equations; AI adds the ability to learn from history, to handle many variables at once and to detect subtle drift early. The same models support real time release testing, where quality is confirmed from in process measurements rather than from samples tested afterwards. That is the step with the biggest payoff and the most regulatory scrutiny.

The regulatory shape

Agencies have issued guidance on continuous manufacturing that expects a defined control strategy, understanding of how disturbances propagate, and rules for diverting material that falls out of limits. AI models inside the control strategy need validation proportionate to their role, and model updates are changes to the process. Because continuous lines are designed with control in mind from the start, they are often the easiest place to bring AI into the control loop properly, with the monitoring and records built in rather than retrofitted.
